findings.finding:
Round 4 fixes R3-1 exactly as required. The token rules now read every command-line word the way systemd v256's parse_proc_cmdline_item does. But PID 1 takes its default unit, and the units it starts, from more than those words. Each of the following inputs is set by an ordinary, quote-free command-line word, and the model ACCEPTS all of them (each probe rebinds every capture).

Kernel side (Linux v6.12 init/main.c). unknown_bootoption hands an unknown KEY=value word whose key has no '.' to init's environment (envp_init). set_init_arg hands every word after '--' to init's argv. run_init_process passes both to the initramfs /init and to /sbin/init.

(a) Environment, the robust case. systemd_efi_options_variable (src/basic/efivars.c) returns $SYSTEMD_EFI_OPTIONS before the SystemdOptions cache. read_efi_options_variable's comment says this env var is checked 'even when in SecureBoot mode'. proc_cmdline_parse (src/basic/proc-cmdline.c) parses it before /proc/cmdline. PID 1's environ survives startup (fixup_environment changes only TERM and HOME) and survives switch-root (do_reexecute uses execv).
- Probe E3: ENROLLED is the positive's line plus ' SYSTEMD_EFI_OPTIONS=systemd.unit=planeon-maintenance.target'. It is ACCEPTED. Because the enrolled entry names no unit, as the README requires, systemd boots planeon-maintenance.target. This works with a systemd initrd and with Secure Boot.
- $SYSTEMD_PROC_CMDLINE (proc_cmdline_strv_internal) replaces /proc/cmdline for PID 1 and for its generators. Generators fork from PID 1, and exec-util do_execute only adds variables. Probe E4 (ENROLLED with SYSTEMD_PROC_CMDLINE=systemd.unit=planeon-maintenance.target) and probe M-b (MAINTENANCE plus SYSTEMD_PROC_CMDLINE=systemd.unit=multi-user.target) are both ACCEPTED.

(b) PID 1 argv. parse_argv (src/core/main.c) runs after parse_configuration's proc_cmdline_parse. It honours --unit (a required_argument option in src/basic/getopt-defs.h) for PID 1, so it overrides the command line.
- Probes E1 and E2 (ENROLLED plus ' -- --unit=planeon-maintenance.target' or ' -- --unit planeon-maintenance.target') and probe M-a (MAINTENANCE plus ' -- --unit=multi-user.target') are ACCEPTED.
- The effect on the host depends on the initrd. Without an initrd, or with an initrd that forwards its argv, host PID 1 boots that unit. With a systemd initrd, the initrd's default unit is set instead, and filter_args drops --unit at switch-root.

(c) Generator inputs (src/debug-generator/debug-generator.c).
- systemd.wants=<unit> adds Wants=<unit> to the default unit (generate_wants_symlinks). Probe E5, ENROLLED plus ' systemd.wants=planeon-maintenance.target', is ACCEPTED, although a word of the enrolled entry names the target.
- systemd.set_credential_binary=systemd.unit-dropin.<unit>:<base64> is imported by src/core/import-creds.c proc_cmdline_callback, and process_unit_credentials writes it as a drop-in. Probe E6 injects 'Wants=planeon-maintenance.target' into multi-user.target. It is ACCEPTED, and no word contains the target name, so no rule based on the target's name can refuse it.
- Probe M-c: MAINTENANCE plus systemd.mask=planeon-maintenance.target is ACCEPTED, but the masked target cannot start.

Scope: the K1 discriminator itself is unaffected (distinct entry IDs and command lines, with every capture bound to the enrolled line's hash; K-a to K-d are refused). Like R2-1 and R3-1, this is an analysis error on observed data in the token rules, and it defeats their stated purpose: the enrolled entry never starts the maintenance target, and the maintenance entry selects it.
The following README sentences are therefore inaccurate:
- the K1 row's 'its default unit is the last of the systemd.unit= values and the SysV runlevel words';
- decision 2's 'read as systemd v256 reads them';
- the model comment at line 249;
- the K1 statement's remedy 'W03 must run Secure Boot', which does not cover $SYSTEMD_EFI_OPTIONS.
This is the third round in which the enumeration of systemd's selectors was incomplete.

questionAnswers.Q3:
All four facts hold in Linux v6.12, and the four README digests match the files fetched at tag v6.12.
- Attach types: 22 census types plus 7 hooks equal to_cgroup_bpf_attach_type's 28 types plus BPF_LSM_CGROUP, which is exactly the set of uapi attach types containing CGROUP.
- Effective query: __cgroup_bpf_query with BPF_F_QUERY_EFFECTIVE copies cgrp->bpf.effective[atype], and spans CGROUP_LSM_START..CGROUP_LSM_END (CGROUP_LSM_NUM 10) for BPF_LSM_CGROUP. compute_effective_progs adds ancestor programs when the ancestor has BPF_F_ALLOW_MULTI or when no nearer program exists.
- pids.current: pids_can_fork charges 1 per task, pids_release uncharges, and 'current' reads the counter.
- /proc/<pid>/exe: exec_binprm replaces bprm->file with bprm->interpreter, set_mm_exe_file records it, and proc_exe_link returns it.
The R4-1 kernel facts come from v6.12 init/main.c: unknown_bootoption sends KEY=value words to envp_init and bare words to argv_init, set_init_arg passes words after '--' to argv, and run_init_process passes both.

reviewLimit:
This is a source-level, DATA_CHECK_ONLY review of the five subject files at commit 824c054 (tree bee1c927). The files were hash-verified at the start and the end of the review.
It establishes no native qualification. It establishes no kernel, SELinux, cgroup, BPF, boot-loader, systemd, initrd or TPM behaviour, no installed profile, selected distribution or seccomp filter, and no E01-E12 obligation. It authorizes nothing.
The kernel and systemd facts come from reading the Linux v6.12 and systemd v256 sources, not from running them. Where an effect depends on the initrd type (R4-1(b)), that is stated.
Repository tests and validators were not run. The v3 model was executed only from byte-identical copies, through my own scripts in /private/tmp/claude-501/w02af-review4/. The v2 model was diffed, not executed.
The out-of-subject working-tree edits were not reviewed. Only the repository, my scratch directory and public source URLs were accessed. No GitHub, runner, sudo, cloud, native or warm-source action was taken.
